themes.title: Anthropic's record IPO resets frontier-AI finance
themes.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, well above the planned $70-78 range, and the enlarged deal collected $81bn-plus with a private placement taking the total toward $107bn - topping SpaceX as the biggest public listing ever and valuing the Claude maker above $1 trillion. The print gives the AI sector its first public price discovery, and the Japan tranche closed at the low end of its range, a hint of where international appetite starts to soften.
themes.angle: First public price tag on a frontier lab - watch global allocation, not just the headline.

themes.title: Nvidia leadership shock ripples into Gulf AI plans
themes.summary: Nvidia beat forecasts and raised its outlook, but stocks still oscillated: the board has ruled out Jensen Huang's return against his stated wish, interim CEO Colette Kress is steering morale and investment, and the company halted China shipments of US-licensed chips. For the Gulf, Fortune frames export controls and the leadership handover as the key watchpoints on UAE and Saudi AI investments.
themes.angle: Gulf boards should treat single-vendor compute risk as a macro exposure, not procurement.

themes.title: AI-speed patching blamed for new tech outages
themes.summary: Experts blame a rush to patch software flaws found by AI for a fresh wave of instability hitting Microsoft, JPMorgan and others, as systematised bug discovery outruns change control. Axios frames the outages as the first true wave of AI-era operational failure, and a Chase software bug delayed payments at other banks.
themes.angle: AI's speed of vulnerability discovery turns patch governance into a board-level risk.

themes.title: Compute economics: capex, cheaper inference, clouds
themes.summary: Capital is still chasing compute: CoreWeave's co-founder prefers spending on capacity over buying back high-yield debt, and Gulf wealth is positioned to shield data centres from a funding squeeze. On cost, DeepMind shipped Gemini 4 Neon as a cheaper alternative to Carbon, while a Harvard tally put US data-centre emissions near Denmark's and sovereign-cloud ties broaden via a US-Malaysia pact.
themes.angle: Capacity, debt and power are the binding constraints - not model quality.
